newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria enters currency board with 2.7 bln marks.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria enters currency board with 2.7 bln marks.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) will start the currency board system on July 1 with 2.7 billion mark gross foreign exchange reserves to cover BNB liabilities of 2.2 trillion levs, head of the BNB Issue Department Martin Zaimov said.

"We have sufficient cover for our lev liabilities," Martin Zaimov, also a BNB deputy governor said in an interview with Reuters and Reuters Financial Television. "The aggregate amount is 2.7 billion German marks and that consists of gold, foreign currency and foreign securities."

The liabilities of the national bank are estimated at 2.2 billion marks or 2.2 trillion Bulgarian levs, said Zaimov. Those comprise the deposits of banks, deposits of the government and the levs in circulation.
The first balance sheet of the issue department will be published on Tuesday afternoon, he said.

Under the currency board, to be launched on Tuesday, the central bank pledges that it will have one German mark for every one thousand levs, freezing the exchange rate at that level. -- Elisaveta Konstantinova, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-981-4145
